extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers and intellectuals interested in science, philosophy, and the public influence of ideas (readers of Popular Science Monthly, scholars of philosophy and science)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria for assessing the merits, influence, and quality of a large-scale philosophical system (here applied to Herbert Spencer's 'synthetic philosophy'), emphasizing scientific conformity, truth, utility, and educative power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness / Ambition
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Herbert Spencer's philosophy can claim to be the most comprehensive, or rather ambitious, of English philosophies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work's scope and ambition are merits: a philosophy that attempts a sweeping synthesis of diverse domains (psychology, biology, sociology, ethics) is to be commended. The editorial praises such largeness as an educational and intellectual achievement and as a reason for broad influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific character / Conformity with science
rubrics_metrics.description: 'It not only "speaks the language of science," but it embodies the truths of science, it organizes the principles of science, it conforms to the methods of science.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong philosophical system should be continuous with scientific knowledge — using scientific generalizations, methods, and verified principles. Identification with science in spirit, substance, and method is given as a primary ground for a system's credibility and influence; anti-patterns include philosophies that repudiate scientific method or remain purely speculative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthfulness / Commitment to truth
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Philosophy, as he views it, is not merely a skillfully reasoned body of speculation; it is nothing, if not true — nothing, unless it compels assent as the highest of verities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Truthfulness is a core standard: a philosophy must aim at established or demonstrable truth and 'compel assent.' Systems that trade on empty speculation or treat truth as secondary fail this test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive synthesis / Organizational power
rubrics_metrics.description: The synthetic philosophy is 'predominantly constructive — a binding together of different orders of ideas by far-reaching principles' and 'the formation of such a philosophy implied a reorganization of knowledge' to bring diverse branches into higher coordination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess a system by its ability to organize and unify disparate domains of knowledge into a coherent whole. The editorial values systematic reorganization that yields greater consistency and congruity as knowledge expands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility / Practical value for human welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: Spencer's system 'is sharply contrasted with preceding philosophical systems by its recognition of the great value of knowledge for useful ends' and 'finds that the highest truth involves also the highest good.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A philosophy should have bearings on human conduct and social policy — supplying guidance for individual liberty, the duties of the state, and moral regulation. The useful, practical consequences of a theory (how it improves human welfare) are an explicit criterion of merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological rigor / Adoption of scientific method in general ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: The system 'conforms to the methods of science' and 'carries its method into the field of general ideas.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond content, the approach and method matter: philosophers should employ rigorous, scientific modes of argument and evidence even when addressing high-level, general, or metaphysical issues. Systems that apply scientific method to philosophy gain respect and influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance and application of the doctrine of evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Dr. Fairbairn 'accepts the doctrine of evolution... the creational method is here held to be evolutional' and Spencer 'first expounded [evolution] as a universal law, developed as a method of thought, and carried out in its main applications.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For philosophies addressing biology, society, and religion, correctly integrating a general evolutionary/developmental framework is treated as essential. Use of evolution as a central explanatory principle is presented as a decisive strength of Spencer's system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicative clarity and intelligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Spencer's system is described as 'so little metaphysical, so concrete, intelligible, real, it so speaks the language of science, is made so striking by brilliant generalizations, and so vivid by abundant, even superabundant illustrations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity, concrete presentation, vivid generalizations, and plentiful illustrative examples enhance a philosophy's persuasive power and accessibility. Overly abstruse or purely metaphysical presentation is an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational power / Capacity to influence and educate an age
rubrics_metrics.description: 'To conceive a system so positive and universal as Mr. Spencer's is itself an education to an age' and the system 'has become one of the most widening, elevating, and potent educative agencies of the age.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One should evaluate whether a philosophical system exerts broad cultural or educational influence — shaping public thought, curricula, and intellectual habits. Influence that leads to the reorientation of other disciplines is a mark of significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical/moral bearing — final aim toward ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Each division (First Principles, Biology, Psychology, Sociology) is 'only so many foundations for the ultimate exposition of the "Principles of Ethics."' The system aims to determine 'the regulation of human conduct.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A major criterion is whether the system meaningfully addresses ethical questions and supplies a coherent moral framework grounded in its theoretical principles. Philosophies that do not connect to prescriptive or normative implications are seen as incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness under criticism / Endurance through controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: Despite being 'pronounced worthless and impotent' and repeatedly 'ostentatiously "crushed,"' Spencer's fabric 'stands the stronger for every attack' and 'becoming more stable with each addition.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a system survives critique and controversy — whether it is refined and strengthened by challenges rather than collapsing. Longevity and the capacity to withstand serious opposition are signs of substantive merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness in critical engagement (anti-pattern for critics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The editorial censures critics who 'often wrote with passion, and indulged in the tone of depreciation wholly foreign to the purposes of honorable controversy' — 'gross personal disparagement' is condemned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While this is guidance for reviewers rather than for the philosophical system itself, it sets a standard for scholarly critique: assessments should be fair, avoid personal attacks, and focus on reasoned argument. Personal disparagement is identified as an improper mode of criticism that should not be practiced.
